messages:
Jon Miller: Quick sync on pinning behavior before the next SDK cut. Proposal: 6-week deprecation window, clear fallback semantics, and diagnostic headers. Need final signoff.

Alex Chen: Quick q: fallback within same model family or to a cross-family default? Family-preserving seems safer.

Maria Lopez: Strongly prefer same-family fallback. Different families can change tokenization/behavior and break clients. Also we should surface which model resolved in diagnostics.

Sara Patel: Can we add a header toggle for strict mode? e.g. `X-Redwood-Pinning: strict|prefer`

Jon Miller: Proposed semantics:
- `strict` => return 409 if exact model:version unavailable
- `prefer` => try pinned version, then family-equivalent, then global default; always return `x-redwood-resolved-model`
- absent header => default is `prefer` with a 2-week soft-grace before auto-migrating

Alex Chen: For the 409 path include `available_versions` and a short migration hint. Also we should publish a tiny JSON schema for that error so clients can parse safely.

Maria Lopez: 6 weeks total ok if we provide migration tooling. Suggest timeline: 2w notice, 4w enforced migration window, then auto-route unless `strict` is set.

Sara Patel: We need a CLI/infra audit to show who is pinned and impact. Suggest `rwd-infer audit --org <org> --since 30d --dry-run`.

Jon Miller: @infra-bot please add task for audit + CLI prototype.

infra-bot: Task INF-7482 created. ETA: 5 working days to add audit endpoint, 10 working days for CLI prototype. Will include `--dry-run`.

Alex Chen: Response shape constraint: do not alter outer `choices` list or primary response fields during fallback. Any extra info must be in `debug` or behind a query param.

Maria Lopez: Docs example for header + response:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-redwood-resolved-model: gptx-medium:v2.3
content-type: application/json

{
  "id": "resp_123",
  "choices": [ {"text": "..."} ],
  "debug": { "fallback_path": ["gptx-medium:v2.3","gptx-medium:latest"] }
}
```

Sara Patel: SDK suggestion: add `client.resolvePin()` helper that simulates routing and returns the model that would be used so integrators can test before flipping traffic.

Jon Miller: Action items:
- Jon: draft JSON schema for 409 and docs (TODAY)
- Alex: RFC for header semantics (tomorrow)
- Maria: product comms + org targeting list (EOD)
- Sara: propose SDK `resolvePin()` surface + tests (tomorrow)
- infra-bot: audit endpoint + CLI prototype (ETA ~2w)

Alex Chen: I'll add the RFC link here when it's up. Will scrub for edge cases (cached KV, streaming difference) :thumbsup:

Maria Lopez: Product will prepare in-console banners for orgs with pinned usage and email cadence at weeks 4 and 5.

Sara Patel: SDK will use the audit endpoint in `--dry-run` to validate client migrations. Tests will include a simulated 409.

infra-bot: INF-7482 updated: branch `pinning-audit/cli-proto` created. CLI will include `--dry-run` flag.

deploy-bot: Heads up: staging deploy for `pinning-audit` infra scheduled in ~2h. Monitor deploy logs.

Jon Miller: If no objections to 6-week plan, I'll proceed with PRs. Will ping for reviews. If someone needs a longer window speak now.

Alex Chen: Minor ask: define the exact `x-redwood-resolved-model` format in docs (family:name:version?) so SDKs can parse reliably.

Maria Lopez: Agreed. Also include migration examples and suggested map from old versions to new ones.

Sara Patel: +1. I'll prototype `resolvePin()` returning `{resolved_model, would_error, hint}`.

Jon Miller: Thanks everyone. I'll open the PR for the error schema and docs this afternoon and link it here. :wave:
